summary: Subhadradis Diskul (1923–2003) was a scholar of history and archaeology. Educated at Chulalongkorn, the École du Louvre under Philippe Stern, and UCL, he held posts at the Bangkok National Museum, Silpakorn University, SEAMEO SPAFA, and the Siam Society.

Subhash Kak (born 1947) works in Indology and engineering. He earned degrees from NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi under Pavaguda V. Indiresan, later serving as a professor at Louisiana State University from 1979 and Regents Professor at Oklahoma State University from 2007.

Subrata K. Mitra (born 1949) studied at Utkal University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Rochester. His academic appointments include positions at the University of Hull, University of Nottingham, Heidelberg University (c. 1994–2014), and National University of Singapore (2015–2018).

Sucheng Chan (born 1941) is a history and Asian American studies scholar. She completed degrees at Swarthmore College, the University of Hawaiʻi, and UC Berkeley, and served as emerita professor at UC Santa Barbara, where she taught from circa 1984 to 2002.

Sudhakara Dvivedi (1855–1910) was an Indologist who studied under Devakrishna. He served as librarian and later professor and head of mathematics and astrology at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Sanskrit College and University between 1883 and 1910.

Sudhir Kakar (1938–2024) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Trained at Gujarat, Mannheim, the Sigmund-Freud-Institut, and Vienna, he held posts at IIM Ahmedabad, IIT Delhi, and INSEAD, along with numerous international visiting professorships and fellowships.

Sue Hamilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned her D.Phil from the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson, and was affiliated with King's College London (attested 2001–2003).

Suehiro Tanemura (1933–2004) studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1953 to 1957. He subsequently held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (circa 1972–1982) and Kokugakuin University (circa 1982–1998).

Suk Fun Ng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Y. Karunadasa, having also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

Sukhlal Sanghvi (1880–1978) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Balakrishna Mishra. He served as professor of Indian philosophy at Gujarat Vidyapith and held the Chair of Jain Philosophy at Banaras Hindu University from 1934 to 1944.

Sukumar Sen (1900–1992) was an Indian linguist and Indologist. Educated at Burdwan Raj College, Sanskrit College, and Calcutta University under Suniti Kumar Chatterji and Irach Taraporewala, he became lecturer (1930) and Khaira Professor (1954) at Calcutta University.

Sukumari Bhattacharji (1921–2014) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University, and held academic posts at Lady Brabourne College (from 1945) and Jadavpur University (1957–1986).

Sulak Sivaraksa (born 1933) is an activist and scholar of Buddhist studies and history. Educated at Lampeter and SSRC, he served as an editor, held visiting posts at Berkeley, Harvard, Lampeter, Toronto, and Cornell, and founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists.

Sumanapala Galmangoda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as Senior Professor at the University of Kelaniya and Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007, 2012).

Sumathi Ramaswamy (born 1961) is a historian and Indologist. She studied at Delhi University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Pennsylvania, and held academic positions at the University of Pennsylvania (1993–1999) and the University of Michigan (1999–2007).
Sumi Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Alexander L. Mayer and a PhD at UCLA (attested 2014) under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Sumitra Mangesh Katre (1906–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD from the University of London. He held posts at Sir Parashurambhau College, Deccan College (Chair of Indo-European Philology, 1942–1971), and the University of Texas at Austin.

Sun-Ah Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago, where she studied under Juhyung Rhi, Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.

Sung Bae Park (born 1933) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctorate under Lewis Lancaster. He served as an assistant professor at Dongguk University and joined the faculty at Stony Brook University in 1977.

Sungdoo Ahn is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Director at Geumgang University and became a professor at Seoul National University (attested 2013).
